extracted.intended_audience: Researchers eligible for appointment to a long-term professorship (habilitated or equivalent), including junior professors, Emmy Noether alumni, junior-group leaders, DFG project staff, mid-level faculty, returning German researchers, and appropriately qualified foreign researchers seeking careers in Germany
extracted.subtask_description: Information and formal requirements for applying to the DFG Heisenberg Programme, including who is eligible/ineligible, available funding types, duration, required forms, and submission/contact procedures. Targets researchers preparing for senior academic roles in Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: To enable outstanding researchers who meet all the requirements for appointment to a long-term professorship to prepare for a senior academic role while continuing their research work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While you prepare for a future senior academic role, the DFG provides funding to enable you to carry on with high-quality research at the institution of your choice and continue building your academic reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers in all disciplines who have qualified for a professorship by completing the habilitation or an equivalent qualification and who have a track record of outstanding research work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directed primarily at researchers who have qualified for professorship via routes such as the Emmy Noether Programme, leadership of a junior research group, DFG project staff positions, private-sector research or mid-level faculty positions; also includes junior professors with positive evaluations and German researchers returning from abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible: Tenure-track and comparable permanent positions in Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: Tenure-track professors in Germany and individuals holding a permanent position in Germany comparable with W2/W3 salary grades are not eligible to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible: researchers who already hold a full professorship abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers from abroad who have already achieved a full professorship are not eligible to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target group / typical backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Programme is directed primarily at researchers who have qualified for professorship via the Emmy Noether Programme, leadership of a junior research group, DFG project staff positions, private-sector research or mid-level faculty positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The target group also includes junior professors who have received positive evaluations, those who have achieved their habilitation or an equivalent qualification, and German researchers returning from abroad, as well as appropriately qualified foreign researchers (who have not yet achieved a full professorship) looking to pursue careers in Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of funding available
rubrics_metrics.description: Four different types of funding are available within the Heisenberg Programme: Heisenberg professorship, Heisenberg position, Heisenberg temporary substitute position for clinicians and Heisenberg fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once you have been accepted to the Heisenberg Programme, you can select between the four funding types or combine them during the five-year funding period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding duration is up to 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance to the Programme provides a five-year funding period during which funding types can be selected or combined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional funding option for Germany-based projects
rubrics_metrics.description: For projects based in Germany, you can also apply for a research grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal submission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals may be submitted at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no fixed deadlines; submissions are accepted on a rolling basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required forms and programme guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must consult the Guidelines Heisenberg Programme (from 1 January 2018) and use DFG Form 10.50: Starting or Changing Your Heisenberg Grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and guidelines are provided on the programme website (linked). Follow these documents for application and grant-start/change procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacts and administrative support
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information on scientific matters is available from the relevant programme division(s); procedural questions can be directed to named contacts and the fellowship office handles financial-management questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange telephone consultations in advance by e-mail; contact the fellowship office during your fellowship for financial-management matters (downloadable contact information provided).
